mechanism_detail: Both drugs inhibit platelet aggregation and coagulation through different pathways — additive anticoagulant effect significantly increases bleeding risk.
clinical_effect: Increased risk of serious bleeding including intracranial hemorrhage
alternatives: Acetaminophen for pain relief instead of Aspirin
monitoring: If combination unavoidable, monitor INR closely and watch for signs of bleeding

mechanism_detail: Both increase serotonergic activity. Tramadol inhibits serotonin reuptake and Sertraline blocks SERT. Combined serotonin excess causes Serotonin Syndrome.
clinical_effect: Serotonin Syndrome: hyperthermia, agitation, tremor, myoclonus, potentially fatal
monitoring: Do not combine. If patient already on both, monitor for serotonin syndrome symptoms.

mechanism_detail: Clarithromycin is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor. Atorvastatin is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. Inhibition causes Atorvastatin plasma levels to increase 10-fold.
clinical_effect: Severe myopathy and rhabdomyolysis (muscle breakdown, kidney failure)
monitoring: If unavoidable: temporarily discontinue statin during antibiotic course

mechanism_detail: Iodinated contrast can cause acute kidney injury. Metformin is renally cleared. AKI leads to Metformin accumulation causing potentially fatal lactic acidosis.
clinical_effect: Lactic acidosis — potentially fatal metabolic emergency
alternatives: Hold Metformin 48hrs before contrast procedure, resume only after kidney function confirmed normal

mechanism_detail: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2 which metabolizes Theophylline. Theophylline plasma levels increase dramatically.
clinical_effect: Theophylline toxicity: seizures, cardiac arrhythmias, nausea, vomiting
monitoring: If combination used: reduce Theophylline dose by 30-50%, monitor serum levels

mechanism_detail: NSAIDs reduce renal prostaglandins causing decreased renal blood flow and reduced Lithium excretion. Lithium accumulates to toxic levels.
clinical_effect: Lithium toxicity: tremor, confusion, seizures, cardiac arrhythmias
alternatives: Acetaminophen/Paracetamol for pain (does not affect Lithium levels)
monitoring: Monitor Lithium serum levels closely if NSAID unavoidable

mechanism_detail: Both drugs cause vasodilation through different mechanisms (PDE5 inhibition vs NO release). Combined effect causes profound, potentially fatal hypotension.
clinical_effect: Severe hypotension: syncope, myocardial infarction, death
alternatives: No safe combination. Patient must choose one or the other.
monitoring: Absolute contraindication. If patient uses nitrates for angina, sildenafil is contraindicated.

mechanism_detail: Fluoxetine inhibits serotonin reuptake. MAOIs block serotonin degradation. Combined: massive serotonin accumulation.
clinical_effect: Severe Serotonin Syndrome: hyperthermia >41C, rhabdomyolysis, DIC, death
alternatives: 14-day washout after stopping MAOI before starting Fluoxetine. 5-week washout after stopping Fluoxetine before starting MAOI.

mechanism_detail: Amiodarone inhibits P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 which eliminates Digoxin. Digoxin levels increase significantly.
clinical_effect: Digoxin toxicity: bradycardia, heart block, ventricular arrhythmias, nausea
alternatives: If combination required, reduce Digoxin dose by 50% and monitor levels closely
monitoring: Monitor Digoxin serum levels and ECG. Target lower end of therapeutic range.

mechanism_detail: Both drugs inhibit dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) enzyme. Combined folate antagonism causes severe myelosuppression.
clinical_effect: Severe bone marrow suppression: pancytopenia, serious infections, bleeding
alternatives: Use different antibiotic class (avoid all antifolates with Methotrexate)
monitoring: If unavoidable: daily folate supplementation, weekly CBC monitoring

mechanism_detail: Rifampin is a potent inducer of CYP2C9, which metabolizes Warfarin. This leads to significantly decreased Warfarin levels.
clinical_effect: Decreased anticoagulation efficacy, increased risk of thrombosis
alternatives: Increase Warfarin dose with close monitoring
monitoring: Monitor INR daily when starting or stopping Rifampin

mechanism_detail: Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C9, decreasing the metabolism of Warfarin.
clinical_effect: Increased INR, high risk of bleeding

mechanism_detail: Ketoconazole inhibits CYP3A4 and P-gp, both involved in Rivaroxaban clearance.
alternatives: Apixaban (still has interaction, use with caution)

mechanism_detail: Phenytoin induces CYP3A4 and P-gp, increasing the clearance of Apixaban.

alternatives: Counsel patient to avoid herbal supplements

mechanism_detail: Fluoxetine is a potent CYP2D6 inhibitor, which is required to convert Tamoxifen to its active metabolite endoxifen.
clinical_effect: Reduced Tamoxifen efficacy in breast cancer treatment

mechanism_detail: Paroxetine inhibits CYP2D6, which metabolizes Metoprolol.
monitoring: Monitor heart rate and blood pressure

mechanism_detail: Erythromycin inhibits CYP3A4, leading to massive Simvastatin accumulation.
monitoring: Monitor for muscle pain and CK levels

mechanism_detail: Linezolid is a weak MAOI; Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic.
Verapamil inhibits P-gp, reducing renal and non-renal clearance of Digoxin.
alternatives: Switch to Diltiazem (still interacts but less)

mechanism_detail: Gemfibrozil inhibits CYP2C8/9, increasing Glyburide levels.
Beta-blockers can mask symptoms of hypoglycemia (tachycardia) and delay recovery.
Induction of CYP3A4 and P-gp decreases Cyclosporine levels.

alternatives: Reduce dose of both if necessary
monitoring: Monitor respiratory rate and sedation level

mechanism_detail: Fluconazole inhibits CYP3A4, which metabolizes Methadone.
Cimetidine competes for renal tubular secretion.
Antibiotics may alter gut flora that produce Vitamin K and may also inhibit CYP enzymes.
Minimal interaction compared to other macrolides.
CYP2C9 induction (complex interaction initially can increase INR).
clinical_effect: Variable INR, usually decreased over time

mechanism_detail: ACE inhibitors reduce renal Lithium clearance.
Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6 which converts Tramadol to active metabolite.
clinical_effect: Reduced analgesia, increased parent drug (serotonin syndrome risk)

mechanism_detail: Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6 which converts Codeine to Morphine.
NSAIDs reduce ACE inhibitor efficacy and increase renal risk.
clinical_effect: Reduced BP control, acute kidney injury

mechanism_detail: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing conversion of Clopidogrel to active form.
CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibition leads to Colchicine toxicity.
Spironolactone may reduce renal Digoxin clearance.

alternatives: Take vitamins 2h after or 6h before antibiotic

mechanism_detail: Reduced acidity decreases absorption of Ketoconazole/Itraconazole.
SSRIs + NSAIDs = high GI bleed risk.
Possible additive risk of lactic acidosis (rare).
